text:
eva: heads-up: small but consistent parse failures on the akira-lite-int4 canary for the `payment_reminder` tool. ~0.12% of calls fail downstream JSON schema. spike correlated with streaming responses that include emoji in the prompt.
hiro: can you paste raw outputs (raw from the canary stream)?
eva: pasted snippets from the logs (raw payloads):
```
{"tool":"payment_reminder","params":{"user":"alice","amount":"$25","due":"2026-03-22"}}
{"tool":"payment_reminder","params":{"user":"alice","amount":"$25","due":"2026-03-22"}} ✓
{"tool":"payment_reminder","params":{"user":"alice","amount":"$25","due":"2026-03-22"}}
```
leila: interesting — second line is valid JSON then a trailing checkmark glyph. that will break strict parsers. emoji getting emitted as a separate token is suspicious, esp. under int4 subtokenization/rounding.
hiro: my hypothesis: the configured eos sentinel is a unicode checkmark (✔) at generation end. on float models the tokenizer emits it as single clean token, but int4 quant+tokenizer packing sometimes yields the glyph as a trailing stray token after the json object, due to streaming chunk boundary + sentinel injection. parser sees `} \u2713` and fails.
eva: can we see how frequent the sentinel appears in suffix form vs embedded? telemetry: in the last 24h slice `eos_suffix_incidence=0.14%`, `parse_failures=0.12%` (most map to `eos_suffix`).
leila: immediate mitigations:
- short-term: runtime strip-suffix heuristic for opt-in routes: `repair_strip_suffix: true, max_strip_len: 8, allowed_chars: printable` that will drop up to N trailing chars if the remainder is valid JSON. only 1 retry attempt.
- safer: change route sentinel to ASCII-only sequence for sensitive routes, e.g., `eos_sentinel: "<|END|>"` instead of emoji. this avoids tokenization ambiguity.
hiro: agree. also add route-level `mirror_mode: schema_checked` and `schema_check: jsonschema-lite` so mirror responses must pass basic conformance; mirror responses failing schema should not be accepted as success.
eva: quick canary snippet (will deploy to payment_reminder route):
```
route.payment_reminder:
  model: akira-lite-int4
  streaming: true
  eos_sentinel: "<|END|>"
  repair_strip_suffix: true
  max_strip_len: 8
  repair_allowed: true
  retry_budget: 2
  telemetry: ["funcall.schema_status","funcall.parse_reason","funcall.repair_attempts"]
```
leila: telemetry enums: `funcall.parse_reason = eos_suffix|truncated_value|glue_concat|malformed_json` and `funcall.schema_status = ok|repaired|failed`. add `funcall.repaired_by = none|strip_suffix|fallback` for auditing.
hiro: risk: `strip_suffix` could hide real corruption (e.g., if model appended an extra field value intentionally). constrain repair to short suffixes and opt-in tools only. for `payment_reminder` it's low-risk.
eva: I ran a small simulated harness: injected checkmark suffix across 100k samples and ran `strip_suffix` heuristics — parse failures dropped from 0.12% -> 0.01%. false-repair rate observed was 0.002% (i.e., cases where stripping removed meaningful chars).
leila: rollout plan:
1) change canary to `eos_sentinel: "<|END|>"` + enable `repair_strip_suffix` for payment_reminder only
2) enable schema telemetry for 48h 
3) run 200k synthetic harness with mixed emoji/ASCII prompts to validate false-repair < 0.01% and no semantic drift
4) if green, expand sentinel change to other user-facing tools and set `repair_strip_suffix` opt-out default (repair disabled by default)
hiro: owners: eva -> canary config + harness runs, leila -> telemetry+dashboard split (`runtime_success` vs `schema_success`), hiro -> runtime PR for `repair_strip_suffix` implementation and unit tests.
infra-bot: canary scheduled: akira-lite-int4 payment_reminder -> ascii-sentinel + strip-suffix on staging at 2026-03-28T02:00Z.
eva: thanks — I'll post the 12h parse_reason histogram and a small sample of stripped vs original payloads after the canary. :mag:
